name: arc-collinear-dot-connectors
description: Use when an ARC grid has sparse same-colored markers on a uniform background. Connect markers that share rows or columns by coloring the cells between them.
---

# ARC collinear dot connectors

## Trigger
A uniform-background ARC grid contains sparse point markers (often color 7 on 8, or 9 on 1), and the demonstration output adds a third color (observed: 3) in straight segments between aligned markers.

## Rule
For each row and each column, find the marker cells. Between every consecutive pair of markers on that row/column, recolor the intervening background cells with 3. Preserve the marker cells and all other cells. Apply row and column segments together; if segments intersect, the intersection is 3 unless it is itself a marker. No diagonal connections.

## Verification
- Compare a demo: every added 3 should lie strictly between two same-colored markers sharing a row or column.
- On the test, enumerate consecutive aligned marker pairs, fill their gaps, and leave all other cells unchanged.
- Check dimensions and confirm the original marker locations are preserved.

## Evidence / caution
This rule was confirmed by a demo with color-9 markers on color-1 background and its corresponding color-3 row/column gaps, and by a solved test with color-7 markers on color-8 background. Use fresh demonstrations if a later puzzle only superficially resembles this pattern.",
